hero.intro: I build production systems where latency and cost actually matter — full-stack fintech wallets, AI-integrated platforms on the MERN stack, and bilingual Next.js products serving audiences across two continents.

about.label: about
about.heading: I started writing code out of curiosity — and never stopped chasing how things actually work.
paragraphs: Since 2023 I've gone from internship projects to shipping products real users depend on. I care about clean architecture — not because it looks good on a CV, but because messy code makes future-me and everyone else miserable.

I spent a year teaching backend engineering to 30+ developers per cohort, which forced me to understand the why behind every pattern. I thrive in async remote collaboration across distributed teams — and I'm available for an immediate start.

stats.label: Average AI response latency under load

items.summary: Architected Node.js/Next.js services integrating OpenAI GPT-4, ElevenLabs TTS and Google Gemini — sub-300ms latency, ~35% throughput gain via caching, and ~20% lower token cost through structured prompt engineering.
Built scalable Next.js/Express/MongoDB features, lifted Lighthouse from 58→89, secured multi-tenant data with OAuth 2.0 + RBAC, and cut deploys from ~2 hours to under 10 minutes with Docker CI/CD.
Designed a 6-month MERN backend curriculum from scratch for cohorts of 30–36. Avg satisfaction 4.7/5.0; 80%+ of graduates secured developer roles within 3 months.
Mentored 40+ students in React and Git workflows, ran 8 workshops and 2 hackathons, and grew GDSC membership 60% across the year.
Delivered 4 production-style capstone APIs including a full e-commerce REST API and real-time chat deployed to AWS. Awarded certificate of distinction for code quality.
Built responsive Vue.js and React dashboards under agile sprints, introducing reusable component patterns that cut front-end duplication ~15%.

contact.label: let's talk

contact.body: Open to full-time remote roles worldwide and relocation. Immediate start. If your team argues about architecture in pull requests and obsesses over response times — we'll get along.
